claims.statement: Chloris was a minor nymph of spring, flowers and new growth, believed to dwell in the Elysian Fields.
claims.statement_id: Chloris adalah nimfa minor yang dikaitkan dengan musim semi, bunga, dan tumbuhan baru, dan diyakini tinggal di Padang Elysia.
claims.quote: was a minor nymph who was associated with spring, flowers and new growth, believed to have dwelt in the Elysian Fields.

claims.statement: Chloris is the equivalent of the Roman goddess Flora, deity of fertility and vegetation.
claims.statement_id: Chloris adalah padanan dewi Romawi Flora, dewi kesuburan dan tumbuhan.
claims.quote: Chloris is the equivalent of the Roman goddess Flora, a deity presiding over fertility and vegetation.

claims.statement: She was abducted by Zephyrus, god of the west wind.
claims.statement_id: Ia diculik Zephyrus, dewa angin barat.
claims.quote: was abducted by Zephyrus, the god of the west wind

claims.statement: Chloris was the goddess of flowers and a nymph of the Islands of the Blessed; she was the wife of Zephyros the West-Wind and the mother of Karpos, god of fruit. Her Roman name was Flora.
claims.statement_id: Chloris adalah dewi bunga dan nimfa Kepulauan Orang Terberkati; ia istri Zephyros, angin barat, dan ibu Karpos, dewa buah. Nama Romawinya Flora.
claims.quote: KHLORIS (Chloris) was the goddess of flowers and a nymph of the Islands of the Blessed. She was the wife of Zephyros the West-Wind and the mother of Karpos (Carpus), god of fruit.

claims.statement: In the quoted speech her husband filled the garden with flowers and told her to have jurisdiction of the flower.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tuturan yang dikutip, suaminya mengisi kebun mereka dengan bunga dan berkata agar ia memegang wewenang atas bunga.
claims.quote: My husband filled it with well-bred flowers, saying : "Have jurisdiction of the flower, goddess."

claims.statement: In the quoted speech, a flower from the fields of Olenus, unique to her gardens, will grant Juno's wish; Juno touches it, conceives, and Mars is created.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tuturan yang dikutip, dikatakan bahwa bunga dari ladang Olenus, yang khas bagi kebunnya, akan mengabulkan keinginan Juno; Juno menyentuhnya, hamil, dan Mars tercipta.
claims.quote: from the fields of Olenus will grant your wish. It's unique to my gardens. ... Juno feels its touch and at the touch conceives. She bulges, and enters Thrace and west Propontis, and fulfils her wish: Mars [Ares] was created.

claims.statement: The resemblance between the names Flora and Chloris led the later Romans to identify the two divinities.
claims.statement_id: Kemiripan nama Flora dan Chloris membuat orang Romawi kemudian menyamakan kedua dewi itu.
claims.quote: The resemblance between the names Flora and Chloris led the later Romans to identify the two divinities.

claims.statement: In the quoted speech the goddess says she was Chloris and is now called Flora, because Latin speech corrupted a Greek letter of her name.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tuturan yang dikutip, sang dewi berkata bahwa ia dahulu Chloris dan kini disebut Flora, karena ucapan Latin mengubah satu huruf Yunani pada namanya.
claims.quote: I was Chloris, whom am now called Flora. Latin speech corrupted a Greek letter of my name.

claims.statement: Lampetia (also Lampetie) was a daughter of the sun god Helios.
claims.statement_id: Lampetia (juga Lampetie) adalah putri dewa matahari Helios.
claims.quote: also spelled Lampetie, was a daughter of the sun god Helios.

claims.statement: With her sister Phaethusa she guarded her father's cattle and sheep on Thrinacia (Sicily).
claims.statement_id: Bersama saudarinya Phaethusa, ia menjaga kawanan sapi dan domba ayahnya di pulau Thrinacia (Sisilia).
claims.quote: She and her sister Phaethusa watched over their father's prized herds of cattle and sheep on the island of Thrinacia (Sicily).

claims.statement: Lampetia wielded an orichalcum staff and herded the cattle.
claims.statement_id: Lampetia memegang tongkat orichalcum dan menggembalakan sapi.
claims.quote: Lampetia wielded an orichalcum staff and herded the cattle.

claims.statement: In the quoted text the herds are pastured by lovely-haired nymph goddesses named Phaethousa and Lampetie, daughters of the sun-god Hyperion (Helios) and Neaera.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks yang dikutip, kawanan itu digembalakan oleh dewi nimfa berambut indah bernama Phaethousa dan Lampetie, putri dewa matahari Hyperion (Helios) dan Neaera.
claims.quote: They are pastured by goddesses, lovely-haired Nymphai (Nymphs) named Phaethousa (Phaethusa) and Lampetie (Lampetia), whose father is the sun-god Hyperion [Helios] and whose mother is bright Neaera

claims.statement: In the quoted text the animals are seven herds of cows and as many flocks of sheep, fifty beasts in each, with no increase from births and no decrease from deaths.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks yang dikutip, kawanan itu terdiri dari tujuh kawanan sapi dan sebanyak itu pula kawanan domba, masing-masing lima puluh ekor, tanpa tambahan karena kelahiran atau pengurangan karena kematian.
claims.quote: they are Helios'--seven herds of cows and as many fine flocks of sheep. In each herd and each flock there are fifty beasts; no births increase them, no deaths diminish them

claims.statement: According to the encyclopedia, the island of Thrinacia (Sicily) was sacred to Helios; his flocks of oxen and sheep were 350 heads each, never increasing or decreasing, and were attended by his daughters Phaetusa and Lampetia.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ensiklopedia itu, pulau Thrinacia (Sicilia) suci bagi Helios; kawanan sapi dan dombanya masing-masing 350 ekor, tidak bertambah atau berkurang, dan dijaga putri-putrinya Phaetusa dan Lampetia.
claims.quote: The island of Thrinacia (Sicily) was sacred to Helios, and he there had flocks of oxen and sheep, each consisting of 350 heads, which never increased or decreased, and were attended to by his daughters Phaetusa and Lampetia.

claims.statement: In the quoted text Lampetie hurried to Hyperion (Helios) the sun god to tell him that his cattle had been slain.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks yang dikutip, Lampetie bergegas menemui Hyperion (Helios) sang dewa matahari untuk memberi tahu bahwa ternaknya telah dibunuh.
claims.quote: But without delay Lampetie (Lampetia) of the trailing robe sped off to Hyperion [Helios] the sun god to tell him that we had slain his cattle

claims.statement: In Roman mythology, Marica was a nymph, mother of Latinus.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Romawi, Marica adalah nimfa, ibu Latinus.
claims.quote: In Roman mythology, Marica was a nymph, the mother of Latinus.

claims.statement: The sacred forest near Minturnae was dedicated to Marica.
claims.statement_id: Hutan suci dekat Minturnae dipersembahkan kepada Marica.
claims.quote: The sacred forest near Minturnae was dedicated to Marica.

claims.statement: Various Roman authors say she was a form of Diana or Venus.
claims.statement_id: Beberapa penulis Romawi menyebutnya wujud Diana atau Venus.
claims.quote: Various Roman authors claims that she was a form of Diana or Venus.

claims.statement: Marica was a Latin nymph who was worshipped at Minturnae, and a grove on the river Liris was sacred to her.
claims.statement_id: Marica adalah nimfa Latin yang dipuja di Minturnae; sebuah hutan kecil di tepi sungai Liris suci baginya.
claims.quote: a Latin nymph who was worshipped at Minturnae, and to whom a grove was sacred on the river Liris.

claims.statement: She was said to be the mother of Latinus by Faunus.
claims.statement_id: Dikatakan bahwa ia ibu Latinus dari Faunus.
claims.quote: She was said to be the mother of Latinus by Faunus.

claims.statement: Servius remarks that some considered her to be identical with Aphrodite and others with Circe.
claims.statement_id: Servius mencatat bahwa sebagian orang menganggapnya identik dengan Aphrodite dan yang lain dengan Circe.
claims.quote: Servius (ad Aen. l.c. and 12.164) remarks that some considered her to be identical with Aphrodite and others with Circe.

claims.statement: Metope is the Arcadian naiad daughter of the river god Ladon, sister of Daphne.
claims.statement_id: Metope adalah naiad Arkadia, putri dewa sungai Ladon dan saudari Daphne.
claims.quote: Metope, the Arcadian naiad daughter of the river god Ladon, thus sister to Daphne.

claims.statement: Her waters were near Stymphalus in the Peloponnese.
claims.statement_id: Airnya berada dekat kota Stymphalus di Peloponnesos.
claims.quote: Her waters were near the town of Stymphalus in the Peloponnesus.

claims.statement: She married the river god Asopus and bore him 12 or 20 daughters.
claims.statement_id: Ia menikah dengan dewa sungai Asopus dan melahirkan 12 atau 20 putri.
claims.quote: She married the river god Asopus by whom she had several (either 12 or 20) daughters

claims.statement: Metope was the Naiad-nymph of the springs and stream of Metope near the town of Stymphalos in Arkadia (southern Greece).
claims.statement_id: Metope adalah naiad dari mata air dan aliran Metope di dekat kota Stymphalos di Arkadia (Yunani selatan).
claims.quote: METOPE was the Naiad-nymph of the springs and stream of Metope near the town of Stymphalos in Arkadia (southern Greece).

claims.statement: Her waters were probably regarded as the source of the Sikyonian Asopus, the stream of her river-god husband.
claims.statement_id: Airnya kemungkinan dianggap sebagai sumber sungai Asopus dari Sikyon, aliran suaminya.
claims.quote: Her waters were probably regarded as the source of the Sikyonian Asopos (Asopus), the stream of her river-god husband.

claims.statement: In the quoted lyric text, Metope is the maid of flowers who bore Thebe, famous rider of horse, and the speaker's mother's mother came from Stymphalos.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks lirik yang dikutip, Metope disebut gadis bunga yang melahirkan Thebe, penunggang kuda termasyhur, dan nenek dari pihak ibu penutur berasal dari Stymphalos.
claims.quote: From Stymphalos (Stymphalus) [in Arkadia] my mother's mother came, that maid of flowers, Metope, who bore Thebe, famous rider of horse.

claims.statement: In the quoted text, Metope, a daughter of the river Ladon, married the river Asopos and bore two sons, Ismenos and Pelagon, and twenty daughters, of whom Zeus kidnapped one named Aigina.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks yang dikutip, Metope, putri sungai Ladon, menikah dengan sungai Asopos dan melahirkan dua putra, Ismenos dan Pelagon, serta dua puluh putri, di antaranya Aigina yang diculik Zeus.
claims.quote: Metope, herself a daughter of the river Ladon, married him [the river Asopos] and bore two sons, Ismenos (Ismenus) and Pelagon, and twenty daughters, of whom Zeus kidnapped one named Aigina (Aegina).

claims.statement: In the quoted text there were born two sons, Pelasgos and Ismenos, and twelve daughters, among them Korkyra and Salamis.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks yang dikutip, lahir dua putra, Pelasgos dan Ismenos, serta dua belas putri, di antaranya Korkyra dan Salamis.
claims.quote: to whom were born two sons, Pelasgos (Pelasgus) and Ismenos (Ismenus), and twelve daughters, Korkyra (Corcyra) and Salamis

claims.statement: In the quoted text, men who honour rivers have statues made of them, some anthropomorphic and others in bovine form; the Stymphalians attribute a likeness to cattle to Erasinos and Metope.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks yang dikutip, orang yang menghormati sungai membuat patung sungai, sebagian berwujud manusia dan sebagian berbentuk sapi; orang Stymphalus menisbatkan rupa seperti sapi kepada Erasinos dan Metope.
claims.quote: men who honour them, and have statues made of them, in some cases set up anthropomorphic statues, while others give them bovine form. A likeness to cattle is attributed by the Stymphalians to Erasinos and Metope.

claims.statement: Orseis was the naiad of a spring in Thessaly and the mythical ancestor of the Greeks.
claims.statement_id: Orseis adalah nimfa air (naiad) sebuah mata air di Thessalia, Yunani, dan leluhur mitos bangsa Yunani.
claims.quote: was the water-nymph (Naiad) of a spring in Thessalia, Greece, and the mythical ancestor of the Greeks.

claims.statement: According to the Library, Orseis married Hellen, son of Deucalion and Pyrrha.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Bibliotheca, Orseis menikah dengan Hellen, putra Deucalion dan Pyrrha.
claims.quote: According to the Library, Orseis married Hellen, son of Deucalion and Pyrrha

claims.statement: Orseis was the Naiad-nymph of spring of a town in the region of Hellas in Thessalia (northern Greece) and the wife of Hellen, an early king of the Hellenes of northern Greece.
claims.statement_id: Orseis adalah naiad mata air sebuah kota di wilayah Hellas di Thessalia (Yunani utara) dan istri Hellen, raja awal bangsa Hellenes di Yunani utara.
claims.quote: ORSEIS was the Naiad-nymph of spring of a town in the region of Hellas in Thessalia (northern Greece). She was the wife of Hellen, an early king of the Hellenes of northern Greece.

claims.statement: Hellen was the only son of Deukalion and Pyrrha, the two survivors of the Great Deluge; the descendants of Hellen and Orseis would come to rule most of Greece.
claims.statement_id: Hellen adalah putra tunggal Deukalion dan Pyrrha, dua orang yang selamat dari Air Bah Besar; keturunan Hellen dan Orseis kelak memerintah sebagian besar Yunani.
claims.quote: He was the only son of Deukalion and Pyrrha, the two survivors of the Great Deluge. Hellen and Orseis' descendants would come to rule most of Greece.

claims.statement: In the quoted text, Hellen and a Nymphe named Orseis had Doros, Xouthos, and Aiolos.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks yang dikutip, Hellen dan seorang nimfa bernama Orseis memiliki Doros, Xouthos, dan Aiolos.
claims.quote: Hellen and a Nymphe named Orseis had Doros (Dorus), Xouthos (Xuthus), and Aiolos (Aeolus).

claims.statement: Orseis was perhaps a daughter of Okeanos or the River Peneios.
claims.statement_id: Orseis mungkin putri Okeanos atau Sungai Peneios.
claims.quote: Perhaps a daughter of OKEANOS or the River PENEIOS

claims.statement: Pallas was one of the Gigantes, offspring of Gaia born from the blood of the castrated Uranus.
claims.statement_id: Pallas adalah salah satu Gigantes (raksasa), keturunan Gaia yang lahir dari darah Uranus yang dikebiri.
claims.quote: was one of the Gigantes (Giants), the offspring of Gaia, born from the blood of the castrated Uranus.

claims.statement: In the Gigantomachy he was flayed by Athena, who used his skin as a shield.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Gigantomachy, perang para raksasa melawan dewa-dewa Olimpus, ia dikuliti Athena yang memakai kulitnya sebagai perisai.
claims.quote: during the Gigantomachy, the cosmic battle of the Giants with the Olympian gods, he was flayed by Athena, who used his skin as a shield.

claims.statement: Pallas was a Gigante slain by Athena in the war against the gods; she stripped off his goatish skin and made of it a shield (the aigis).
claims.statement_id: Pallas adalah seorang Gigante yang tewas oleh Athena dalam perang melawan para dewa; Athena mengambil kulitnya yang mirip kulit kambing dan menjadikannya perisai (aigis).
claims.quote: A Gigante slain by Athena in the war against the gods. She stripped off his goatish skin and made of it a shield for the battle (the aigis).

claims.statement: In the quoted text, Athena stripped the skin off Pallas and used it to protect her own body during the battle.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks yang dikutip, Athena mengulitinya dan memakai kulitnya untuk melindungi tubuhnya selama pertempuran.
claims.quote: She stripped the skin off Pallas and used it to protect her own body during the battle.

claims.statement: According to some, Pallas was not a Gigante but a Titan opponent of Athena in the earlier Titanomachy.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sebagian, Pallas bukan Gigante melainkan Titan lawan Athena dalam Titanomachy yang lebih awal.
claims.quote: According to some, Pallas was not a Gigante but a Titan opponent of Athena in the earlier Titanomakhia (War of the Titans).

claims.statement: The Gigante Pallas was perhaps the same as the Titan of the same name.
claims.statement_id: Pallas sang Gigante mungkin sama dengan Titan bernama sama.
claims.quote: He was perhaps the same as the Titan of the same name.

claims.statement: Agathos Daimon was originally a lesser deity (daemon) of classical Greek and Graeco-Egyptian religion.
claims.statement_id: Agathos Daimon awalnya dewa kecil (daemon) dalam agama Yunani klasik dan Yunani-Mesir.
claims.quote: originally was a lesser deity (daemon) of classical ancient Greek religion and Graeco-Egyptian religion.

claims.statement: In Greek form he was a household god, offered libations with Zeus Soter after meals.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bentuk Yunani aslinya, ia dewa rumah tangga yang diberi persembahan minuman bersama Zeus Soter setelah makan.
claims.quote: In his original Greek form, he served as a household god, to whom, along with Zeus Soter, libations were made after a meal.

claims.statement: In Ptolemaic times he became a serpentine civic god, special protector of Alexandria.
claims.statement_id: Pada masa Ptolemaios, ia menjadi dewa kota berwujud ular dan pelindung khusus Alexandria.
claims.quote: a prominent serpentine civic god, who served as the special protector of Alexandria

claims.statement: In Greek mythology, Agathodaemon was the good spirit of cornfields and vineyards.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Yunani, Agathodaemon adalah roh baik ladang jagung dan kebun anggur.
claims.quote: in Greek mythology, the "good spirit" of cornfields and vineyards.

claims.statement: It was the custom of the Greeks to drink a cup of pure wine in his honour at the end of each meal.
claims.statement_id: Orang Yunani biasa meminum secawan anggur murni untuk menghormatinya di akhir tiap santapan.
claims.quote: It was the custom of the Greeks to drink a cup of pure wine in his honour at the end of each meal

claims.statement: He was also regarded as the protecting spirit of the state and of individuals.
claims.statement_id: Ia juga dianggap sebagai roh pelindung negara dan individu.
claims.quote: He was also regarded as the protecting spirit of the state and of individuals.

claims.statement: In works of art he is represented as a serpent, or as a young man with a cornucopia and a bowl in one hand and a poppy and ears of corn in the other.
claims.statement_id: Dalam karya seni ia digambarkan sebagai ular, atau pemuda dengan cornucopia dan mangkuk di satu tangan serta bunga poppy dan bulir jagung di tangan lainnya.
claims.quote: He is represented in works of art in the form of a serpent, or of a young man with a cornucopia and a bowl in one hand, and a poppy and ears of corn in the other.

claims.statement: His other role was as a genus of serpentine household gods, the Agathoi Daimones, individual protectors of the homes in which they were worshipped.
claims.statement_id: Peran lain Agathos Daimon adalah sekelompok dewa rumah tangga berbentuk ular, Agathoi Daimones, pelindung masing-masing rumah tempat mereka dipuja.
claims.quote: the other as a genus of serpentine household gods, the Agathoi Daimones, individual protectors of the homes in which they were worshipped.

claims.statement: His origin in Alexandria is disputed: two conflicting views paint him either as a Greek cultural importation later identified with Serapis, or as a Hellenized native Egyptian household god.
claims.statement_id: Asal-usulnya di Alexandria diperselisihkan: dua pandangan yang bertentangan menyebutnya dewa budaya Yunani yang dibawa masuk dan kemudian disamakan dengan Serapis, atau dewa rumah tangga asli Mesir yang dihelenisasi.
claims.quote: His origin in Alexandria is a matter of dispute, with two conflicting views either painting Agathos Daimon as a Greek cultural importation later identified with Serapis ... or as a Hellenized native Egyptian household god.

claims.statement: Cebren was a Greek river god whose river lay near Troy.
claims.statement_id: Cebren adalah dewa sungai Yunani yang sungainya terletak dekat Troya.
claims.quote: was a Greek river-god, whose river was located near Troy.

claims.statement: He was the son of Oceanus and Tethys and father of Asterope and Hesperia.
claims.statement_id: Ia putra Oceanus dan Tethys, dan ayah Asterope dan Hesperia.
claims.quote: He was the son of Oceanus and Tethys and he was the father of Asterope and Hesperia

claims.statement: Kebren (Cebren) was a river-god of the Troad in north-western Mysia, Anatolia.
claims.statement_id: Kebren (Cebren) adalah dewa sungai di wilayah Troad, Mysia barat laut, Anatolia.
claims.quote: KEBREN (Cebren) was a river-god of the Troad in north-western Mysia, Anatolia.

claims.statement: The River Kebren was a tributary of the Skamandros whose headwaters lay in the foothills of Mount Ida near the town of Kebrene.
claims.statement_id: Sungai Kebren adalah anak sungai Skamandros dengan hulu di kaki Gunung Ida dekat kota Kebrene.
claims.quote: The River Kebren was a tributary of the Skamandros (Scamander) whose headwaters lay in the foothills of Mount Ida near the town of Kebrene (Cebrene).

claims.statement: In the quoted text, Alexandros (Paris) married Oinone, daughter of the river Kebren.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks yang dikutip, Alexandros (Paris) menikahi Oinone, putri sungai Kebren.
claims.quote: Alexandros (Alexander) [Paris] married Oinone (Oenone), daughter of the river Kebren (Cebren).

claims.statement: In the quoted text, after Alexandros took Helene to wife, Oinone took his conduct exceedingly ill and returned to Kebren, her father.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks yang dikutip, setelah Alexandros mengambil Helene sebagai istri, Oinone sangat tersinggung dan kembali kepada Kebren, ayahnya.
claims.quote: Alexandros took Helene to wife : Oinone took his conduct exceedingly ill, and returned to Kebren, the author of her days.

claims.statement: In the quoted text, Hesperie, daughter of Cebren, is seen by her father's river bank.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks yang dikutip, Hesperie, putri Cebren, terlihat di tepi sungai ayahnya.
claims.quote: Hesperie Cebrenis (Daughter of Cebren) he saw by her father Cebren's river bank.

claims.statement: Kebren may be the same as the river Heptaporos mentioned by Homer.
claims.statement_id: Kebren mungkin sama dengan sungai Heptaporos yang disebut Homer.
claims.quote: Kebren may be the same as the river Heptaporos mentioned by Homer.

claims.statement: Cymopoleia was a daughter of the sea god Poseidon and wife of Briareus, one of the three Hecatoncheires.
claims.statement_id: Cymopoleia adalah putri dewa laut Poseidon dan istri Briareus, salah satu dari tiga Hecatoncheires.
claims.quote: was a daughter of the sea god Poseidon, and the wife of Briareus, one of the three Hecatoncheires.

claims.statement: Her only known Classical mention is in the Hesiodic Theogony.
claims.statement_id: Satu-satunya penyebutannya dari masa Klasik ada dalam Theogony karya Hesiodos.
claims.quote: Her only known mention in Classical antiquity occurs in the Hesiodic Theogony.

claims.statement: Kymopoleia was a sea-nymph daughter of Poseidon and the wife of the hundred-handed storm-giant Briareos; she was probably a goddess of the violent storm waves generated by her husband.
claims.statement_id: Kymopoleia adalah nimfa laut, putri Poseidon dan istri Briareos, raksasa badai berseratus tangan; ia kemungkinan dewi ombak badai yang dibangkitkan suaminya.
claims.quote: KYMOPOLEIA (Cymopoleia) was a sea-nymph daughter of the god Poseidon and the wife of the hundred-handed, storm-giant Briareos. She was probably a goddess of the violent storm waves generated by her husband.

claims.statement: In the quoted text, Poseidon made Briareos his son-in-law by giving him Kymopoleia, his daughter, to wed.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks yang dikutip, Poseidon menjadikan Briareos menantunya dengan menyerahkan Kymopoleia, putrinya, untuk dinikahi.
claims.quote: Briareos (Briareus), being goodly, the deep-roaring Earth-Shaker [Poseidon] made his son-in-law, giving him Kymopoleia (Cymopoleia) his daughter to wed.

claims.statement: In the quoted text, Kymodoke, with Kymatolege and Amphitrite, easily stills the waves and hushes the winds on the open water.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks yang dikutip, Kymodoke, bersama Kymatolege dan Amphitrite, dengan mudah menenangkan ombak dan meredakan angin di permukaan laut terbuka.
claims.quote: [The Nereid] Kymodoke (Cymodoce) who, with Kymatolege (Cymatolege) and Amphitrite, light of foot, on the misty face of the open water easily stills the waves and hushes the winds in their blowing.

claims.statement: The note says Kymatolege is named in connection with the Nereides but was not numbered among them, and was probably Kymopoleia, daughter of Amphitrite.
claims.statement_id: Catatan itu menyebut Kymatolege dikaitkan dengan para Nereid tetapi tidak dihitung di antara mereka, dan mungkin ia Kymopoleia, putri Amphitrite.
claims.quote: Kymatolege is named in connection with the Nereides but was not numbered amongst them. She was probably Kymopoleia, daughter of Amphitrite, who occurs later in Hesiod.

claims.statement: Himalia was a nymph of the eastern end of Rhodes.
claims.statement_id: Himalia adalah nimfa dari ujung timur pulau Rhodes.
claims.quote: was a nymph of the eastern end of the island of Rhodes.

claims.statement: After subduing the Titans, Zeus fell for Himalia and joined with her as a fertile rain.
claims.statement_id: Setelah menaklukkan para Titan, Zeus jatuh cinta pada Himalia dan menyatu dengannya dalam wujud hujan yang menyuburkan.
claims.quote: after Zeus subdued the Titans, he became enamored with Himalia and mated with her in the form of a fertile rain.

claims.statement: She bore him three sons: Spartaeus, Cronius and Cytus.
claims.statement_id: Mereka memiliki tiga putra: Spartaeus, Cronius, dan Cytus.
claims.quote: The latter produced three sons with him, Spartaeus, Cronius, and Cytus

claims.statement: Himalia was a nymph of the Aegean island of Rhodes; Zeus seduced her when he came to subdue the island's resident Titanes, the Telkhines.
claims.statement_id: Himalia adalah nimfa dari pulau Rhodes di Laut Aegea; Zeus merayunya ketika datang menaklukkan para Titanes penghuni pulau itu, yaitu Telkhines.
claims.quote: HIMALIA was a nymph of the Aegean island of Rhodes. She was seduced by the god Zeus when he came to subdue the island's resident Titanes--the Telkhines.

claims.statement: In the quoted text, Zeus became enamoured of one of the Nymphai, Himalia by name, and begat by her three sons: Spartaios, Kronios, and Kytos.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks yang dikutip, Zeus jatuh cinta pada salah satu nimfa bernama Himalia dan memperanakkan tiga putra: Spartaios, Kronios, dan Kytos.
claims.quote: he became enamoured of one of the Nymphai (Nymphs), Himalia by name, and begat by her three sons, Spartaios (Spartaeus), Kronios (Cronius), and Kytos (Cytus).

claims.statement: Himalia was perhaps identified with Halia, the sister of the Telkhines.
claims.statement_id: Himalia mungkin diidentifikasi dengan Halia, saudari Telkhines.
claims.quote: Himalia was perhaps identified with Halia, the sister of the Telkhines.

claims.statement: The kallikantzaros is a malevolent creature of modern Greek folklore.
claims.statement_id: Kallikantzaros adalah makhluk jahat dalam cerita rakyat Yunani modern.
claims.quote: is a malevolent creature in modern Greek folklore.

claims.statement: They live underground trying to saw down the giant tree that supports the earth, but surface during the twelve days of Christmas, 25 December to 6 January.
claims.statement_id: Kallikantzaroi diyakini tinggal di bawah tanah dan berusaha menggergaji pohon raksasa penyangga bumi, tetapi naik ke permukaan selama dua belas hari Natal, 25 Desember hingga 6 Januari.
claims.quote: Kallikantzaroi are believed to dwell underground spending most of the time trying to saw down the giant tree that supports the earth, but come to the surface during the twelve days of Christmas, from 25 December to 6 January

claims.statement: Equivalents occur in Bulgarian folklore.
claims.statement_id: Padanannya ada dalam cerita rakyat Bulgaria.
claims.quote: Its equivalents occur in Bulgarian

claims.statement: For the rest of the year they live in the lower world and try to gnaw through or cut down the great tree (or one or more columns) on which the world rests.
claims.statement_id: Selama sisa tahun mereka hidup di dunia bawah dan berusaha menggerogoti atau menebang pohon besar (atau satu atau beberapa tiang) tempat dunia bertumpu.
claims.quote: The rest of the year they live in the lower world, and occupy themselves in trying to gnaw through or cut down the great tree (or in other accounts the one or more columns) on which the world rests.

claims.statement: Each Christmas the task is nearly done when the time comes for them to appear in the upper world, and during their twelve days' absence the supports of the world are made whole again.
claims.statement_id: Tiap Natal tugas itu hampir selesai ketika tiba saat mereka naik ke dunia atas, dan selama dua belas hari mereka pergi, penopang dunia pulih kembali.
claims.quote: Each Christmas they have nearly completed their task, when the time comes for their appearance in the upper world, and during their twelve days' absence, the supports of the world are made whole again.

claims.statement: From dawn until sunset they hide in dark and dank places, in caves or beneath mills, and feed on worms, snakes, frogs, tortoises and other unclean things.
claims.statement_id: Dari fajar hingga senja mereka bersembunyi di tempat gelap dan lembap, di gua atau di bawah kincir, dan makan cacing, ular, katak, kura-kura, serta hal-hal tak bersih lain.
claims.quote: From dawn till sunset they hide themselves in dark and dank places—in caves or beneath mills—and there feed on such food as they can collect, worms, snakes, frogs, tortoises, and other unclean things.

claims.statement: They swarm into homes by chimney and door, overturn and break all the furniture, devour the Christmas pork, and befoul the water, wine and food that remain.
claims.statement_id: Mereka menyerbu rumah lewat cerobong dan pintu, menjungkirbalikkan dan mematahkan semua perabot, menyantap daging babi Natal, dan mengotori air, anggur, serta makanan yang tersisa.
claims.quote: By chimney and door alike they swarm in, and make havoc of the home; in sheer wanton mischief they overturn and break all the furniture, devour the Christmas pork, befoul all the water and wine and food which remains

claims.statement: Their faces are black, their eyes glare red, they have the ears of goats or asses, and blood-red tongues loll from their huge mouths, flanked by ferocious tusks.
claims.statement_id: Wajah mereka hitam, mata merah menyala, bertelinga kambing atau keledai, dan lidah merah darah menjulur dari mulut besar mereka, diapit taring garang.
claims.quote: Their faces are black; their eyes glare red; they have the ears of goats or asses; from their huge mouths blood-red tongues loll out, flanked by ferocious tusks.

claims.statement: Hence it is not surprising that they are often lame, but even so they are swift of foot and terrible in strength.
claims.statement_id: Karena itu tidak mengherankan bila mereka sering pincang, tetapi meski begitu mereka cepat berlari dan sangat kuat.
claims.quote: Hence it is not surprising that they are often lame, but even so they are swift of foot and terrible in strength.

claims.statement: At the crowing of the third cock, who is black and more potent to scare away demons than the white and red cocks who precede him, they vanish away, like all terrors of the night.
claims.statement_id: Pada kokok ayam jantan ketiga, yang hitam dan lebih ampuh menakuti setan daripada ayam putih dan merah sebelumnya, mereka lenyap, seperti semua kengerian malam.
claims.quote: For at that sound (or, to be more precise, at the crowing of the third cock, who is black and more potent to scare away demons than the white and red cocks who precede him ... they vanish away, like all terrors of the night in ancient

claims.statement: All Callicantzari are essentially mischievous; the mischief of the larger sort is often malicious and even deadly, while the smaller sort are more frolicsome and harmless in their tricks.
claims.statement_id: Semua Callicantzari pada dasarnya jahil; kejahilan jenis yang lebih besar sering berniat buruk dan bahkan mematikan, sedangkan jenis yang lebih kecil lebih jenaka dan tidak berbahaya dalam tipu dayanya.
claims.quote: while all Callicantzari are essentially mischievous in character, the mischief wrought by the larger sort is often of a malicious and even deadly order, while the smaller sort are more frolicsome and harmless in their tricks.

claims.statement: The author states that the explanation for the extraordinary divergences and contradictions in accounts of the Callicantzari lies in their identity with the ancient Centaurs.
claims.statement_id: Sang penulis menyatakan bahwa penjelasan atas keanehan dan pertentangan dalam uraian tentang Callicantzari terletak pada identitas mereka dengan Centaur kuno.
claims.quote: The extraordinary divergences and even contradictions in different accounts of the Callicantzari demand ... That explanation, as I shall show later, lies in their identity with the ancient Centaurs.

claims.statement: Larunda was a naiad, daughter of the river Almo and mother of the Lares Compitalici, guardians of the crossroads and Rome.
claims.statement_id: Larunda adalah naiad, putri sungai Almo dan ibu Lares Compitalici, penjaga persimpangan jalan dan kota Roma.
claims.quote: was a naiad nymph, daughter of the river Almo and mother of the Lares Compitalici, guardians of the crossroads and the city of Rome.

claims.statement: Ovid's Fasti is the only known mythography of Larunda.
claims.statement_id: Fasti karya Ovidius adalah satu-satunya sumber mitos tentang Larunda.
claims.quote: Ovid's Fasti provides the only known mythography attached to Larunda.

claims.statement: Jupiter tears out Lara's tongue and orders Mercury to take her to the infernal marshes of Avernus.
claims.statement_id: Jupiter mencabut lidah Lara dan menyuruh Mercurius membawanya ke rawa neraka Avernus.
claims.quote: Jupiter wrenches out Lara's tongue and orders Mercury, psychopomp and god of boundaries and transitions, to conduct her to the "infernal marshes" of Avernus

claims.statement: Larunda, or Lara, a daughter of Almon, was a nymph who denounced to Juno that there was some connexion between Jupiter and Juturna.
claims.statement_id: Larunda atau Lara, putri Almon, adalah nimfa yang melaporkan kepada Juno bahwa ada hubungan antara Jupiter dan Juturna.
claims.quote: or LARA, a daughter of Almon, was a nymph who denounced to Juno that there was some connexion between Jupiter and Juturna

claims.statement: Jupiter punished her by depriving her of her tongue and condemning her to be conducted into the lower world by Mercury; on the way Mercury fell in love with her, and afterwards she gave birth to two Lares.
claims.statement_id: Jupiter menghukumnya dengan mencabut lidahnya dan menyuruh Mercury membawanya ke dunia bawah; di jalan Mercury jatuh cinta padanya, dan kemudian ia melahirkan dua Lares.
claims.quote: Jupiter punished her by depriving her of her tongue, and condemning her to be conducted into the lower world by Mercury ;but on the way thither Mercury fell in love with her, and afterwards she gave birth to two Lares.

claims.statement: Hartung infers from Lactantius that Larunda is identical with Muta and Tacita.
claims.statement_id: Hartung menyimpulkan dari Lactantius bahwa Larunda identik dengan Muta dan Tacita.
claims.quote: Hartung (Die Relig. der Röm. ii. p. 204) infers from Lactantius (1.20) that Larunda is identical with Muta and Tacita.

claims.statement: Monopods were mythological dwarf-like creatures with a single large foot on a central leg.
claims.statement_id: Monopod adalah makhluk mitos mirip kurcaci dengan satu kaki besar yang keluar dari tungkai di tengah tubuhnya.
claims.quote: were mythological dwarf-like creatures with a single, large foot extending from a leg centred in the middle of their bodies.

claims.statement: Monopods appear in Aristophanes' The Birds, first staged in 414 BC.
claims.statement_id: Monopod muncul dalam drama Aristophanes, The Birds, yang pertama kali dipentaskan tahun 414 SM.
claims.quote: Monopods appear in Aristophanes' play The Birds, first performed in 414 BC.

claims.statement: Pliny the Elder describes them in his Natural History from travelers' tales of Monopods in India.
claims.statement_id: Plinius Tua menggambarkan mereka dalam Natural History berdasarkan cerita pelancong tentang Monopod di India.
claims.quote: They are described by Pliny the Elder in his Natural History, where he reports travelers' stories from encounters or sightings of Monopods in India.

claims.statement: The Skiapodes (Sciapods) were a tribe of one-legged, giant-footed Ethiopian or Indian men who raised their large foot into the air for shade against the hot southern sun.
claims.statement_id: Skiapodes (Sciapods) adalah suku laki-laki berkaki satu dan berkaki raksasa dari Etiopia atau India yang mengangkat kaki besarnya ke udara sebagai peneduh dari terik matahari selatan.
claims.quote: THE SKIAPODES (Sciapods) were a tribe of one-legged, giant-footed Ethiopian or Indian men who raised their large foot into the air for shade against the hot southern sun.

claims.statement: In the quoted passage the Monocoli (One-Legged) have only one leg and move in jumps with surprising speed; they are also called Sciapodes (Shadow-Foots) because in the hotter weather they lie on their backs and protect themselves with the shadow of their feet.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan itu, Monocoli (Berkaki Satu) berkaki satu dan bergerak dengan lompatan secepat mengejutkan; mereka juga disebut Sciapodes (Berkaki Bayangan) karena saat cuaca lebih panas mereka berbaring telentang dan berlindung dengan bayangan kaki mereka.
claims.quote: Monocoli (One-Legged) who have only one leg, and who move in jumps with surprising speed; the same are called Sciapodes (Shadow-Foots) tribe, because in the hotter weather they lie on their backs on the ground and protect themselves with the shadow of their feet.

claims.statement: In the quoted passage a speaker states that the Skiapodes or Long-Headed men, and other poetical fancies recounted about them in a treatise, did not live anywhere on the earth, least of all in India.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan itu, seorang narasumber menyatakan bahwa orang Skiapodes atau berkepala panjang, dan hal-hal khayali lain dalam sebuah risalah tentang mereka, tidak hidup di mana pun di bumi, apalagi di India.
claims.quote: As to men that are Skiapodes (Shadow-Footed) or Makrokephaloi (Macrocephali) (Long-Headed), and as to the other poetical fancies which the treatise of Skylax recounts about them, he said that they didn't live anywhere on the earth, and least of all in India.

claims.statement: In the quoted passage the Skiapodes are listed among the tribes of Aithiopia (Ethiopia).
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan itu, Skiapodes termasuk suku-suku Aithiopia (Etiopia).
claims.quote: The Nasamones and the Androphagoi (Man-Eaters) and the Pygmaioi (Pygmies) and Skiapodes (Sciapods) (Shadow-Foots) people are also tribes of Aithiopia (Ethiopia)

claims.statement: The Skiapodes were also popular in medieval bestiaries and map illustrations of Terra Incognita.
claims.statement_id: Skiapodes juga populer dalam bestiari abad pertengahan dan ilustrasi peta Terra Incognita.
claims.quote: The Skiapodes were also popular in Medieval bestiaries and map illustrations of Terra Incognita.

claims.statement: Mormo was a female spirit of Greek folklore whose name mothers and nurses invoked to scare children into behaving.
claims.statement_id: Mormo adalah roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Yunani yang namanya dipakai ibu dan pengasuh untuk menakuti anak-anak agar tidak nakal.
claims.quote: was a female spirit in Greek folklore, whose name was invoked by mothers and nurses to frighten children to keep them from misbehaving.

claims.statement: The plural mormones means "fearful ones" and relates to words meaning "fright".
claims.statement_id: Bentuk jamak mormo adalah mormones, "yang menakutkan", terkait kata-kata bermakna "ketakutan".
claims.quote: The name mormo has the plural form mormones which means "fearful ones" or "hideous one(s)", and is related to an array of words that signify "fright".

claims.statement: In a quoted poem the Mormo made children tremble: on its head were huge ears, it walked on all fours, and it changed from one face to another.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan sebuah puisi, Mormo membuat anak-anak gemetar: kepalanya bertelinga besar, ia berjalan merangkak, dan berganti dari satu wajah ke wajah lain.
claims.quote: Oh, what a trembling the Mormo brought us then, when we were little ones!--On its head were huge ears, and it walked on all fours, and changed from one face to another!

claims.statement: In a quoted play a speaker made dizzy by terrifying armor begs that "that Mormo (Bogy-Monster)" be taken away.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan sebuah lakon, seorang pembicara yang pusing melihat baju zirah menakutkan memohon agar "Mormo (hantu penakut)" disingkirkan.
claims.quote: Your terrifying armor makes me dizzy. I beg you, take away that Mormo (Bogy-Monster)!

claims.statement: In the quoted passage someone is urged not to fear death as if it were a Mormolykeion (Hobgoblin).
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan itu, orang diminta tidak takut mati seolah-olah kematian itu Mormolykeion (hantu penakut).
claims.quote: Try to persuade him not to fear death as if it were a Mormolykeion (Hobgoblin).

claims.statement: The Mormolyceia were said to be able to assume the form of beautiful women to lure young men to bed, where they sucked their blood and consumed their flesh.
claims.statement_id: Mormolyceia dikatakan dapat mengambil wujud wanita cantik untuk memikat pemuda ke ranjang, lalu menghisap darah dan memakan daging mereka.
claims.quote: The Mormolyceia further were said to be able to assume the form of beautiful women for the purpose of luring young men to bed, where they sucked their blood and consumed their flesh.

claims.statement: The Mormolyceion is the same phantom or bugbear as Mormo and is used for the same purpose.
claims.statement_id: Mormolyceion adalah momok yang sama dengan Mormo dan dipakai untuk tujuan yang sama.
claims.quote: or MORMOLYCEION ... the same phantom or bugbear as Mormo, and also used for the same purpose.

claims.statement: Mormo was one of the same class of bugbears as Empusa and Lamia.
claims.statement_id: Mormo termasuk golongan momok yang sama dengan Empusa dan Lamia.
claims.quote: Mormo was one of the same class of bugbears as Empusa and Lamia.

claims.statement: According to an account attested in only a single source, the original Mormo was a woman of Corinth who ate her children and then flew away.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sebuah catatan yang hanya terbukti dalam satu sumber, Mormo asli adalah perempuan Korintus yang memakan anak-anaknya lalu terbang pergi.
claims.quote: The original Mormo was a woman of Corinth, who ate her children then flew away, according to an account only attested in a single source.

claims.statement: Simoeis was a river of the Trojan plain, now the Dümruk Su, and the name of its god in Greek mythology.
claims.statement_id: Simoeis adalah sungai di dataran Troya, kini Dümruk Su, sekaligus nama dewanya dalam mitologi Yunani.
claims.quote: was a river of the Trojan plain, now called the Dümruk Su (Dümrek Çayı), and the name of its god in Greek mythology.

claims.statement: The Iliad often mentions it as a rapid mountain torrent.
claims.statement_id: Sungai ini sering disebut dalam Iliad sebagai aliran gunung yang deras.
claims.quote: This river is frequently spoken of in the Iliad, and described as a rapid mountain torrent.

claims.statement: Simoeis was a river god of the Troad in north-western Anatolia (modern Turkey); his river was a tributary of the Skamandros and the two streams merged near the city of Troy.
claims.statement_id: Simoeis adalah dewa sungai di Troad, Anatolia barat laut (Turki modern); sungainya anak sungai Skamandros dan keduanya bertemu dekat kota Troy.
claims.quote: SIMOEIS was a River-God of the Troad in north-western Anatolia (modern Turkey). The Simoeis was a tributory of the river Skamandros (Scamander). Their two streams merged near the city of Troy.

claims.statement: In the quoted epic passage the Skamandros calls aloud upon Simoeis, "beloved brother", to join in holding back the strength of a man who will storm the great city of Priamos.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan epos, Skamandros memanggil Simoeis "saudara tercinta" dan mengajaknya bergabung menahan kekuatan seorang pria yang akan menyerbu kota besar Priamos.
claims.quote: But [the River] Skamandros did not either abate his fury ... and called aloud upon Simoeis : 'Beloved brother, let even the two of us join to hold back the strength of a man, since presently he will storm the great city of lord Priamos (Priam).

claims.statement: In the quoted passage the Skamandros asks Simoeis to help beat the man off by filling his currents from his springs, rousing all his torrents and making a big wave rear up.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan itu, Skamandros meminta Simoeis membantu mengusir orang itu dengan memenuhi arusnya dari mata air, menggerakkan semua derasnya, dan menegakkan gelombang besar.
claims.quote: But [the River] Skamandros did not either abate his fury ... But help me beat him off with all speed, and make full your currents with water from your springs, and rouse up all your torrents and make a big wave rear up

claims.statement: According to the dictionary, Simoeis was a son of Oceanus and Tethys and the father of Astyoche and Hieromneme.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kamus itu, Simoeis putra Oceanus dan Tethys serta ayah Astyoche dan Hieromneme.
claims.quote: He is described as a son of Oceanus and Tethys ... and as the father of Astyoche and Hieromneme.

claims.statement: In the quoted epic passage Hera stays her horses, slipping them from the chariot, and Simoeis grows ambrosia as grass for them to graze on.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan epos, Hera menghentikan kudanya dan melepaskannya dari kereta, dan Simoeis menumbuhkan rumput ambrosia untuk dimakan kuda-kuda itu.
claims.quote: there the goddess of the white arms, Hera, stayed her horses, slipping them from the chariot ... and Simoeis grew as grass ambrosia for them to graze on.

claims.statement: In the quoted passage Dardanos, first king of Troy, has given the firstling crop of his hair to Phrygian Simoeis.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan itu, Dardanos, raja pertama Troya, mempersembahkan potongan pertama rambutnya kepada Simoeis dari Phrygia.
claims.quote: He [Dardanos first king of Troy] has given the firstling crop of his hair to Phrygian Simoeis.

claims.statement: Thalia was a nymph, daughter of Hephaestus and mother of the Palici.
claims.statement_id: Thalia adalah nimfa putri Hephaestus dan ibu para Palici.
claims.quote: was a nymph daughter of Hephaestus, and the mother of the Palici.

claims.statement: She buried herself in the ground to escape Hera's jealousy.
claims.statement_id: Ia mengubur dirinya di tanah untuk menghindari kecemburuan Hera.
claims.quote: She buried herself in the ground to avoid Hera's jealousy.

claims.statement: Her twins, the Palici, were thus born under the earth.
claims.statement_id: Karena itu anak kembarnya, para Palici, lahir di bawah tanah.
claims.quote: Her twin children, the Palici, were thus born under the earth

claims.statement: Thaleia was a Naiad-nymph of Mount Aitna (Etna) in Sicily; Zeus loved her, but fearing the wrath of Hera she asked to be hidden beneath the earth.
claims.statement_id: Thaleia adalah naiad Gunung Aitna (Etna) di Sisilia; Zeus mencintainya, tetapi karena takut akan murka Hera ia meminta disembunyikan di bawah tanah.
claims.quote: THALEIA was a Naiad-nymph of Mount Aitna (Etna) in Sicily. She was loved by the god Zeus but, fearing the wrath of Hera, asked to be hidden beneath the earth.

claims.statement: Beneath the earth she gave birth to the Palikoi (Palici), twin Sicilian gods of hot springs and geysers.
claims.statement_id: Di bawah tanah ia melahirkan Palikoi (Palici), dewa kembar Sisilia penguasa mata air panas dan geyser.
claims.quote: There she gave birth to the Palikoi (Palici)--twin Sicilian gods of hot springs and geysers.

claims.statement: In the plot summary a Sicilian maiden named Thaleia or Aitna, embraced by Zeus, prayed in fear of Hera's wrath that the earth might open and swallow her up; her prayer was granted, and when the time of her delivery was at hand the earth opened again and twin boys came forth.
claims.statement_id: Dalam ringkasan alur itu, seorang gadis Sisilia bernama Thaleia atau Aitna, yang dipeluk Zeus, berdoa agar bumi terbuka dan menelannya karena takut murka Hera; doanya dikabulkan, dan ketika tiba waktunya melahirkan, bumi terbuka lagi dan keluarlah anak kembar laki-laki.
claims.quote: A Sicilian maiden named Thaleia or Aitna (Aetna), having been embraced by Zeus, in fear of Hera's wrath prayed that the earth might open and swallow her up. Her prayer was granted, but when the time of her delivery was at hand, the earth opened again and twin boys came forth

claims.statement: The Palikoi were Sicilian daemons, twin sons of Zeus and the Nymph Thaleia, the daughter of Hephaestus.
claims.statement_id: Palikoi adalah daimon Sisilia, putra kembar Zeus dan nimfa Thaleia putri Hephaestus.
claims.quote: The Palikoi were Sicilian daemons, twin sons of Zeus and the Nymph Thaleia, the daughter of Hephaestus.

claims.statement: The Tiburtine Sibyl, also called Albunea, was a Roman sibyl seated at ancient Tibur (modern Tivoli).
claims.statement_id: Sibyl Tiburtina, juga disebut Albunea, adalah peramal perempuan Romawi yang berkedudukan di kota kuno Tibur (kini Tivoli).
claims.quote: The Tiburtine Sibyl, also called Albunea, was a Roman sibyl, whose seat was the ancient town of Tibur (modern Tivoli).

claims.statement: Augustus's mythic meeting with the Sibyl, asking whether he should be worshipped as a god, was often painted from the late Middle Ages on.
claims.statement_id: Pertemuan mitis Augustus dengan Sibyl, saat ia bertanya apakah dirinya harus disembah sebagai dewa, sering dilukis seniman sejak akhir Abad Pertengahan.
claims.quote: The mythic meeting of Augustus with the Sibyl, of whom he inquired whether he should be worshiped as a god, was often depicted by artists from the late Middle Ages onwards.

claims.statement: In the quotation, the Tiburtine Sibyl, by name Albunea, is worshiped at Tibur as a goddess near the banks of the Anio, in which stream her image is said to have been found holding a book; the Senate transferred her oracular responses to the Capitol.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan itu, Sibyl Tiburtina, bernama Albunea, dipuja di Tibur sebagai dewi dekat tepi sungai Anio, tempat patungnya dikatakan ditemukan sedang memegang buku; tanggapan orakelnya dipindahkan Senat ke Capitol.
claims.quote: The Tiburtine Sibyl, by name Albunea, is worshiped at Tibur as a goddess, near the banks of the Anio, in which stream her image is said to have been found, holding a book in her hand. Her oracular responses the Senate transferred into the capitol.

claims.statement: In the later medieval versions the Sibyl answers Augustus by showing him a vision of a young woman with a baby boy high in the sky, and a voice from the heavens says that this is the virgin who shall conceive the saviour of the world.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi Abad Pertengahan akhir, sang Sibyl menjawab Augustus dengan memperlihatkan penglihatan seorang perempuan muda dengan bayi laki-laki di langit, dan suara dari langit berkata bahwa itulah perawan yang akan mengandung juru selamat dunia.
claims.quote: In the versions known to the later Middle Ages, such as the account in the Golden Legend, Augustus asked the Sibyl whether he should be worshipped as a god ... She replied by showing him a vision of a young woman with a baby boy high in the sky, and a voice from the heavens said, "This is the virgin who shall conceive the saviour of the world"

claims.statement: Albunea was a prophetic nymph or Sibyl; near Tibur a grove with a well and a temple was consecrated to her, and near it was the oracle of Faunus Fatidicus.
claims.statement_id: Albunea adalah nimfa atau sibyl peramal; di sekitar Tibur hutan kecil dengan mata air dan kuil dipersembahkan kepadanya, dan di dekatnya ada orakel Faunus Fatidicus.
claims.quote: a prophetic nymph or Sibyl, to whom in the neighbourhood of Tibur a grove was consecrated, with a well and a temple. Near it was the oracle of Faunus Fatidicus.

claims.statement: Her oracles, which belonged to the libri fatales, were at the command of the senate deposited and kept in the Capitol.
claims.statement_id: Ramalannya, yang termasuk libri fatales, atas perintah senat disimpan di Capitol.
claims.quote: Her series, or oracles, which belonged to the libri fatales, were, at the command of the senate, deposited and kept in the Capitol.

claims.statement: An apocalyptic pseudo-prophecy among the Sibylline Oracles was attributed to the Tiburtine Sibyl.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah pseudo-nubuat apokaliptik di antara Sibylline Oracles dikaitkan dengan Sibyl Tiburtina.
claims.quote: An apocalyptic pseudo-prophecy exists among the Sibylline Oracles, which was attributed to the Tiburtine Sibyl.

claims.statement: In Roman mythology, Volturnus was a god of the Tiber, perhaps of all rivers.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Romawi, Volturnus adalah dewa Sungai Tiber dan mungkin dewa semua sungai.
claims.quote: In Roman mythology, Volturnus was a god of the Tiber, and may have been the god of all rivers.

claims.statement: He had his own priest, the Flamen Volturnalis, and his festival, the Volturnalia, was on August 27.
claims.statement_id: Ia punya imam sendiri, Flamen Volturnalis, dan perayaannya, Volturnalia, diadakan pada 27 Agustus.
claims.quote: He had his own minor flamen, a high priest, the Flamen Volturnalis. His festival, Volturnalia, was held on August 27.

claims.statement: Originally Etruscan, his worship spread to Rome.
claims.statement_id: Awalnya ia dewa Etruria, lalu pemujaannya menyebar ke Roma.
claims.quote: Although he was originally an Etruscan god, his worship spread to Rome

claims.statement: According to a dictionary, Fontus, believed to be a son of Janus, was a brother of Volturnus.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sebuah kamus, Fontus, yang dianggap putra Janus, adalah saudara Volturnus.
claims.quote: believed to be a son of Janus. ... He was a brother of Volturnus.

claims.statement: Two quoted lines preserve the names of six flamens appointed by Numa according to the poet, including Volturnalem.
claims.statement_id: Dua baris yang dikutip menyimpan nama enam flamen yang diangkat Numa menurut sang penyair, termasuk Volturnalem.
claims.quote: preserve the names of six of these, appointed, says the poet, by Numa, — Volturnalem, Palatualem, Furinalem,

claims.statement: Volturnus had a daughter Juturna and a grandchild Fons, the god of spring water, born of a love affair between Juturna and Janus.
claims.statement_id: Volturnus punya anak perempuan Juturna dan cucu Fons, dewa mata air, yang lahir dari hubungan Juturna dan Janus.
claims.quote: Volturnus had at least two descendants, a daughter named Juturna, a grandchild named Fons. Fons was born of a love affair between Juturna and Janus, and was the god of spring water.

claims.statement: Arges was one of the three Hesiodic Cyclopes.
claims.statement_id: Arges adalah salah satu dari tiga Cyclops dalam karya Hesiodos.
claims.quote: was one of the three Hesiodic Cyclopes in Greek mythology.

claims.statement: His name means "bright", the brightness of lightning.
claims.statement_id: Namanya berarti "terang", melambangkan cahaya kilat.
claims.quote: His name means "bright" and represents the brightness from lightning.

claims.statement: Arges is a child of Gaia and Uranus, brother of the Cyclopes Brontes and Steropes.
claims.statement_id: Arges anak Gaia dan Uranus; saudaranya termasuk sesama Cyclops Brontes dan Steropes.
claims.quote: Arges is a child of Gaia and Uranus, and his siblings include his fellow cyclopes, Brontes and Steropes

claims.statement: The three elder Kyklopes were orb-eyed, immortal giants who forged the lightning-bolts of Zeus.
claims.statement_id: Tiga Cyclops tua adalah raksasa abadi bermata bulat yang menempa petir Zeus.
claims.quote: THE ELDER KYKLOPES (Cyclopes) were three, orb-eyed, immortal giants who forged the lightning-bolts of Zeus.

claims.statement: In the quoted text Brontes, Steropes and stubborn-hearted Arges gave Zeus the thunder and made the thunderbolt; in all else they were like the gods, but only one eye was set in the midst of their foreheads.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks yang dikutip, Brontes, Steropes, dan Arges yang keras hati memberi Zeus guntur dan membuat petirnya; dalam hal lain mereka seperti para dewa, tetapi hanya satu mata di tengah dahi mereka.
claims.quote: Brontes, and Steropes and stubborn-hearted Arges, who gave Zeus the thunder and made the thunderbolt : in all else they were like the gods, but one eye only was set in the midst of their fore-heads.

claims.statement: In the quoted text strength, might and craft were in their works.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks yang dikutip, kekuatan, tenaga, dan kecerdikan ada dalam karya mereka.
claims.quote: Strength and might and craft were in their works.

claims.statement: Zeus and his brothers later released them, and in return they provided Zeus with his thunderbolts, Poseidon with his storm-raising trident, and Haides with a helm of invisibility.
claims.statement_id: Zeus dan saudara-saudaranya kemudian membebaskan mereka, dan sebagai balasan mereka memberi Zeus petirnya, Poseidon trisula penggerak badai, dan Haides helm yang membuat tak terlihat.
claims.quote: Zeus and his brothers later released them and in return they provided the god with his thunderbolts, Poseidon with his storm-raising trident, and Haides with a helm of invisibility.

claims.statement: As soon as they were born their father Ouranos locked them away inside the belly of Earth along with the Hekatonkheires; when the Titanes overthrew Ouranos they drove the giants into the pit of Tartaros.
claims.statement_id: Begitu lahir, ayah mereka Ouranos mengurung mereka di dalam perut Bumi bersama para Hekatonkheires; ketika para Titan menggulingkan Ouranos, mereka melempar para raksasa itu ke jurang Tartaros.
claims.quote: As soon as they were born, their father Ouranos (Uranus, the Sky) locked them away inside the belly of Earth, along with their stormy brothers, the hundred-handed Hekatonkheires (Hecatoncheires). When the Titanes overthrew Ouranos, they drove the giants into the pit of Tartaros.

claims.statement: According to the dictionary the Cyclopes were afterwards killed by Apollo for furnishing Zeus with the thunderbolts to kill Asclepius; according to others it was not the Cyclopes themselves that were killed but their sons.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kamus itu, para Cyclops kemudian dibunuh Apollo karena menyediakan petir bagi Zeus untuk membunuh Asclepius; menurut yang lain, bukan para Cyclops sendiri yang terbunuh, melainkan putra-putra mereka.
claims.quote: Henceforth they remained the ministers of Zeus, but were afterwards killed by Apollo for having furnished Zeus with the thunderbolts to kill Asclepius. ... According to others, however, it was not the Cyclopes themselves that were killed, but their sons.

claims.statement: In Hesiod's Theogony, Brontes is one of the Cyclopes (with Steropes and Arges), sons of Uranus and Gaia who made Zeus's thunderbolt.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Theogony karya Hesiodos, Brontes adalah salah satu Cyclops (bersama Steropes dan Arges), putra Uranus dan Gaia, pembuat petir senjata Zeus.
claims.quote: In Hesiod's Theogony, the Cyclopes are Brontes, Steropes, and Arges, sons of Uranus and Gaia and creators of Zeus's characteristic weapon, the thunderbolt.

claims.statement: The name Brontes means "Thunder", reflecting their role as thunderbolt makers.
claims.statement_id: Nama Brontes berarti "guntur", mencerminkan peran para Cyclops sebagai pembuat petir.
claims.quote: The names that Hesiod gives them, Arges (Bright), Brontes (Thunder), and Steropes (Lightning), reflect their fundamental role as thunderbolt makers.

claims.statement: Ovid also has Brontes and Steropes working at forges in Sicilian caves.
claims.statement_id: Ovidius juga menggambarkan Brontes dan Steropes bekerja di tempat tempa di gua-gua Sisilia.
claims.quote: The later Latin poet Ovid also has the Hesiodic Cyclopes, Brontes and Steropes (along with a third Cyclops named Acmonides), work at forges in Sicilian caves.

claims.statement: In Hesiod's Theogony (trans. Evelyn-White), the Kyklopes, Brontes, Steropes and stubborn-hearted Arges, gave Zeus the thunder and made the thunderbolt; in all else they were like the gods, but only one eye was set in the middle of their foreheads, and strength, might and craft were in their works.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Theogony karya Hesiodos (terjemahan Evelyn-White), para Kyklopes, yaitu Brontes, Steropes, dan Arges yang berhati keras, memberi Zeus guruh dan membuat petir; dalam segala hal lain mereka seperti para dewa, tetapi hanya satu mata terpasang di tengah dahi mereka, dan dalam karya mereka ada kekuatan, daya, dan kecakapan.
claims.quote: Hesiod, Theogony 139 ff (trans. Evelyn-White) ... the Kyklopes (Cyclopes), overbearing in spirit, Brontes, and Steropes and stubborn-hearted Arges, who gave Zeus the thunder and made the thunderbolt : in all else they were like the gods, but one eye only was set in the midst of their fore-heads. ... Strength and might and craft were in their works.

claims.statement: In Pseudo-Apollodorus' Bibliotheca (trans. Aldrich), Ouranos (Uranus) sired the Kyklopes, named Arges (Flash), Steropes (Lightning) and Brontes (Thunder), each with one eye in his forehead; Ouranos then bound them and threw them into Tartaros (Tartarus).
claims.statement_id: Dalam Bibliotheca karya Pseudo-Apollodorus (terjemahan Aldrich), Ouranos (Uranus) melahirkan para Kyklopes bernama Arges (Kilatan), Steropes (Kilat), dan Brontes (Guruh), masing-masing bermata satu di dahinya; lalu Ouranos membelenggu mereka dan melemparkannya ke Tartaros (Tartarus).
claims.quote: Pseudo-Apollodorus, Bibliotheca 1. 1 - 4 (trans. Aldrich) ... After these he sired the Kyklopes (Cyclopes), by name Arges (Flash), Steropes (Lightning), and Brontes (Thunder), each of whom had one eye in his forehead. But Ouranos (Uranus, Sky) bound these and threw them into Tartaros (Tartarus)

claims.statement: In Pseudo-Apollodorus' Bibliotheca, after Ouranos' rule was overthrown the Titanes retrieved their brothers from Tartaros and gave the power to Kronos, but Kronos once again bound the Kyklopes and confined them in Tartaros.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Bibliotheca karya Pseudo-Apollodorus, setelah Ouranos digulingkan, para Titanes mengeluarkan saudara-saudara mereka dari Tartaros dan menyerahkan kekuasaan kepada Kronos; tetapi Kronos kembali membelenggu para Kyklopes dan mengurung mereka di Tartaros.
claims.quote: Pseudo-Apollodorus, Bibliotheca 1. 1 - 4 (trans. Aldrich) ... Thus having overthrown Ouranos' rule the Titanes retrieved their brothers from Tartaros and gave the power to Kronos. But Kronos once again bound the Kyklopes and confined them in Tartaros.

claims.statement: According to this encyclopedia, the Cyclopes provided Zeus with thunderbolts and lightning, Pluto with a helmet and Poseidon with a trident; afterwards they remained the ministers of Zeus, but were later killed by Apollo for having furnished Zeus with the thunderbolts that killed Asclepius.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ensiklopedia ini, para Cyclops memberi Zeus petir dan kilat, Pluto sebuah helm, dan Poseidon sebuah trisula; sesudahnya mereka tetap menjadi pelayan Zeus, tetapi kemudian dibunuh Apollo karena telah menyediakan petir yang dipakai Zeus untuk membunuh Asclepius.
claims.quote: the Cyclopes provided Zeus with thunderbolts and lightning, Pluto with a helmet, and Poseidon with a trident. ... Henceforth they remained the ministers of Zeus, but were afterwards killed by Apollo for having furnished Zeus with the thunderbolts to kill Asclepius.

claims.statement: In Virgil's Aeneid (trans. Day-Lewis), the Cyclopes were hard at work in an underground iron foundry, Brontes and Steropes with Pyracmon stripped to the buff; they made a thunderbolt of the kind the Father of heaven (Zeus) shoots down in great numbers at the earth from all over the sky.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Aeneid karya Vergilius (terjemahan Day-Lewis), para Cyclops giat bekerja di pandai besi bawah tanah, Brontes dan Steropes bersama Pyracmon yang digambarkan "stripped to the buff"; mereka membuat petir seperti yang ditembakkan Bapa langit (Zeus) ke bumi dalam jumlah besar dari seluruh penjuru langit.
claims.quote: Virgil, Aeneid 8. 418 ff (trans. Day-Lewis) ... The Cyclopes were hard at work in this underground iron-foundry--Brontes and Steropes, Pyracmon stripped to the buff. They manufactured a thunderbolt, such as the Father of heaven [Zeus] shoots down in such great numbers at earth from all over the sky

claims.statement: In Valerius Flaccus' Argonautica (trans. Mozley), the god of Delos (Apollon) pays for having struck down the Cyclops Steropes with his thankless bow.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Argonautica karya Valerius Flaccus (terjemahan Mozley), dewa Delos (Apollon) membayar karena telah menjatuhkan sang Cyclops Steropes dengan busurnya yang tak tahu terima kasih.
claims.quote: Valerius Flaccus, Argonautica 1. 445 ff (trans. Mozley) ... for it is in thy fields that the god of Delos [Apollon] pays for having struck down [the Cylcops] Steropes with his thankless bow.

claims.statement: Liriope is a Boeotian naiad of Thespiae, probably daughter of a Boeotian or Phocian river god.
claims.statement_id: Liriope adalah naiad Boeotia dari Thespiae, mungkin putri salah satu dewa sungai Boeotia atau Phocis.
claims.quote: is a Boeotian naiad of Thespiae, who was probably the daughter of one of the Boeotian or Phocian river gods.

claims.statement: She bore the river god Cephissus a son, Narcissus.
claims.statement_id: Ia melahirkan Narcissus dari dewa sungai Cephissus.
claims.quote: Liriope was raped by the river-god Cephissus, who was himself the son of Pontus and Thalassa, and bore his son Narcissus.

claims.statement: Liriope's name means "face of the narcissus".
claims.statement_id: Nama Liriope berarti "wajah bunga narsis".
claims.quote: Liriope's name means "face of the narcissus" from the Greek words leirion "narcissus" and ops "face."

claims.statement: Liriope was a Naiad nymph of Phokis (in central Greece). She bore the river god Kephisos (Cephisus) a beautiful son named Narkissos (Narcissus), who was transformed into the flower that shares his name.
claims.statement_id: Liriope adalah nimfa naiad dari Phokis (di Yunani tengah). Ia melahirkan seorang putra yang rupawan, Narkissos (Narcissus), dari dewa sungai Kephisos (Cephisus); putranya itu diubah menjadi bunga yang senama dengannya.
claims.quote: LIRIOPE was a Naiad-nymph of Phokis (in central Greece). She bore the river-god Kephisos (Cephisus) a beautiful son named Narkissos (Narcissus) who was transformed into his namesake flower.

claims.statement: Liriope was probably identified with Lilaia, the Naiad nymph of the springs of the river Kephisos.
claims.statement_id: Liriope kemungkinan besar disamakan dengan Lilaia, nimfa naiad mata air sungai Kephisos.
claims.quote: Liriope was probably identified with Lilaia, the Naiad-nymph of the springs of the river Kephisos.

claims.statement: In Ovid's Metamorphoses (trans. Melville), Liriope is the wave-blue water nymph whom Cephisos once embraced and ravished in his winding flow.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Metamorphoses karya Ovidius (terjemahan Melville), Liriope adalah nimfa air berwarna biru ombak yang pernah dipeluk dan dirudapaksa oleh Cephisos dalam alirannya yang berkelok.
claims.quote: Ovid, Metamorphoses 3. 342 ff (trans. Melville) ... Wave-blue water-nymph Liriope, whom once Cephisos in his sinuous flow embracing held and ravished.

claims.statement: In Ovid's Metamorphoses (trans. Melville), the nymph bore a fine infant boy and named him Narcissus. She asked the seer whether he would enjoy long years and a ripe old age, and was answered: 'If he shall himself not know.'
claims.statement_id: Dalam Metamorphoses karya Ovidius (terjemahan Melville), sang nimfa melahirkan seorang putra yang menawan dan menamainya Narcissus. Ia bertanya kepada peramal apakah anaknya akan menikmati umur panjang, dan dijawab: "Jika ia sendiri tidak mengenal dirinya."
claims.quote: Ovid, Metamorphoses 3. 342 ff (trans. Melville) ... the lovely Nymphe bore a fine infant boy, from birth adorable, and named her son Narcissus; and of him she asked the seer ... would he long years and ripe old age enjoy, who answered ‘If he shall himself not know.’

claims.statement: Macris is a daughter of Aristaeus who raised the young Hera before incurring her wrath and being banished.
claims.statement_id: Macris adalah putri Aristaeus yang mengasuh dewi Hera saat muda, sebelum dimurkai dan diusir oleh sang dewi.
claims.quote: is a daughter of Aristaeus who reared the goddess Hera in her youth, before incurring the wrath of the goddess and being banished by her.

claims.statement: Macris was a daughter of Aristaeus, a rustic god and son of Apollo; she was also called Nysa.
claims.statement_id: Macris putri Aristaeus, dewa pedesaan dan putra Apollo; ia juga disebut Nysa.
claims.quote: Macris was a daughter of Aristaeus, a rustic god and son of Apollo. She was also called Nysa.

claims.statement: Makris (Macris) was a nymph, daughter of the rustic god Aristaios (Aristaeus), who nursed the infant Dionysos in a cave on the island of Euboia.
claims.statement_id: Makris (Macris) adalah nimfa putri dewa pedesaan Aristaios (Aristaeus) yang mengasuh Dionysos yang masih bayi di sebuah gua di pulau Euboia.
claims.quote: MAKRIS (Macris) was a nymph daughter of the rustic-god Aristaios (Aristaeus) who nursed the infant Dionysos in a cave on the island of Euboia.

claims.statement: She was later driven from her home by the wrathful goddess Hera and settled on Korkyra, home of the Phaiakes (Phaeacians).
claims.statement_id: Ia kemudian diusir dari rumahnya oleh dewi Hera yang murka dan menetap di Korkyra, tempat tinggal bangsa Phaiakes (Phaeacians).
claims.quote: She was later driven from her home by the wrathful goddess Hera and settled on Korkyra (Corycra), home of the Phaiakes (Phaeacians).

claims.statement: In Apollonius Rhodius' Argonautica, Makris in Euboia took the infant Dionysos to her bosom and moistened his parched lips with honey, after Hermes had rescued him from the flames and brought him to her.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Argonautica karya Apollonius Rhodius, Makris di Euboia mengambil bayi Dionysos ke dadanya dan membasahi bibirnya yang kering dengan madu, setelah Hermes menyelamatkan sang bayi dari api dan membawanya kepadanya.
claims.quote: Apollonius Rhodius, Argonautica 4. 1128 ff ... It was Makris, who in Abantian Euboia (Euboea), took the infant Dionysos to her bosom and moistened his parched lips with honey, when Hermes had rescued him from the flames and brought him to her.

claims.statement: In the Argonautica, Hera saw this and in her anger banished Makris from Euboia. Makris came to the remote Phaiakian land, where she lived in the sacred cave and brought abundance to the people.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Argonautica, Hera melihat hal itu dan dalam amarahnya mengusir Makris dari Euboia. Makris pun tiba di negeri Phaiakia yang jauh, tinggal di gua suci, dan membawa kelimpahan bagi penduduknya.
claims.quote: Apollonius Rhodius, Argonautica 4. 1128 ff ... But Hera saw this and in her anger banished her from Euboia. So Makris came to the remote Phaiakian land, where she lived in the sacred cave and brought abundance to the people.

claims.statement: Makris' name was derived from the Greek word makros, meaning "far away", or makaria, meaning "blessed".
claims.statement_id: Nama Makris berasal dari kata Yunani makros yang berarti "jauh" atau makaria yang berarti "diberkati".
claims.quote: Makris' name was derived from the Greek word makros meaning "far away" or makaria meaning "blessed".

claims.statement: Makris was also known as Nysa and in this guise was often multiplied into a troupe of Nysiades.
claims.statement_id: Makris juga dikenal sebagai Nysa, dan dalam wujud ini ia sering digandakan menjadi sekelompok Nysiades.
claims.quote: Makris was also known as Nysa and in this guise was often multiplied into a troupe of Nysiades.

claims.statement: In Diodorus Siculus' Library of History, Ammon (Zeus) came and brought the child (Dionysos) and gave him into the care of Nysa, one of the daughters of Aristaios.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Library of History karya Diodorus Siculus, Ammon (Zeus) datang membawa sang anak (Dionysos) dan menyerahkannya kepada Nysa, salah satu putri Aristaios.
claims.quote: Diodorus Siculus, Library of History 3. 70. 1 (trans. Oldfather) ... Ammon [Zeus] came and brought the child [Dionysos] and gave him into the care of Nysa, one of the daughters of Aristaios (Aristaeus)

claims.statement: According to Wikipedia, Hermes or Zeus himself later took the infant Dionysus to Macris, who nursed him and fed him honey.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wikipedia, Hermes atau Zeus sendiri kemudian membawa Dionysus yang masih bayi kepada Macris, yang menyusuinya dan memberinya madu.
claims.quote: Some time later, Hermes or Zeus himself took the infant Dionysus and brought him to Macris, who nursed him and fed him honey.

claims.statement: Podarge is a harpy, personification of a swift wind and mate of Zephyrus, the West Wind.
claims.statement_id: Podarge adalah harpy, personifikasi angin cepat dan pasangan Zephyrus, angin barat.
claims.quote: is a harpy, a personification of a swift wind and mate of Zephyrus, the West Wind.

claims.statement: She is the mother of Balius and Xanthus, two swift divine horses given to Achilles.
claims.statement_id: Ia ibu Balius dan Xanthus, dua kuda dewa yang terkenal cepat dan dihadiahkan kepada Achilles.
claims.quote: She is the mother of Balius and Xanthus — two divine horses renowned for their swiftness and who were gifted to Achilles

claims.statement: In Homer's Iliad (trans. Lattimore), Xanthos and Balios, horses that raced with the speed of the winds, were conceived by stormy Podarge (a Harpy) of Zephyros (the West Wind) and borne as she grazed in the meadow beside the swirl of Okeanos.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Iliad karya Homeros (terjemahan Lattimore), Xanthos dan Balios, kuda-kuda secepat angin, dikandung oleh Podarge yang berbadai (seorang harpy) dari Zephyros (angin barat) dan dilahirkannya saat ia merumput di padang di tepi pusaran Okeanos.
claims.quote: Homer, Iliad 16. 148 ff (trans. Lattimore) ... Xanthos (Xanthus) and Balios (Balius), who tore with the winds' speed, horses stormy Podarge [a Harpyia (Harpy)] once conceived of Zephyros (the West Wind) and bore, as she grazed in the meadow beside the swirl of Okeanos (Oceanus).

claims.statement: In Stesichorus' Fragment 178 (from the Etymologicum Magnum), Hermes gave the Dioskouri Phlogeus and Harpagos, swift foals of Podarge, while Hera gave them Xanthos and Kyllaros.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Fragmen 178 Stesichorus (dikutip dari Etymologicum Magnum), Hermes memberi para Dioskouri Phlogeus dan Harpagos, anak kuda yang cepat milik Podarge, sedangkan Hera memberi mereka Xanthos dan Kyllaros.
claims.quote: Stesichorus, Fragment 178 (from Etymologicum Magnum) ... Stesichorus in his Funeral Games of Pelias says that Hermes gave the Dioskouri (Dioscuri) ... Phlogeus and Harpagos, swift foals of Podarge, while Hera gave them Xanthos (Xanthus) and Kyllaros (Cyllarus).

claims.statement: According to this encyclopedia, in the Homeric poems the Harpies ("the swift robbers") are nothing but personified storm winds, and Homer names only one, Podarge, who was married to Zephyrus and gave birth to Achilles' two horses, Xanthus and Balius.
claims.statement_id: Menurut ensiklopedia ini, dalam puisi-puisi Homeros para harpy ("perampas yang cepat") tak lebih dari angin badai yang dipersonifikasikan, dan Homeros hanya menyebut satu nama, yaitu Podarge, yang menikah dengan Zephyrus dan melahirkan dua kuda Achilles, Xanthus dan Balius.
claims.quote: HARPYIAE (Harpuiai), that is, "the swift robbers," are, in the Homeric poems, nothing but personified storm winds. ... Homer mentions only one by name, viz. Podarge, who was married to Zephyrus, and gave birth to the two horses of Achilles, Xanthus and Balius.

claims.statement: The Harpyiai (Harpies), the kind of being to which Podarge belongs, were the spirits (daimones) of sudden, sharp gusts of wind. They were known as the hounds of Zeus and were despatched by the god to snatch people and things away from the earth.
claims.statement_id: Para Harpyiai (harpy), golongan makhluk tempat Podarge termasuk, adalah roh (daimones) embusan angin yang tiba-tiba dan tajam. Mereka dikenal sebagai anjing pemburu Zeus yang diutus untuk menyambar orang dan benda dari bumi.
claims.quote: THE HARPYIAI (Harpies) were the spirits (daimones) of sudden, sharp gusts of wind. They were known as the hounds of Zeus and were despatched by the god to snatch away ... people and things from the earth.

claims.statement: The Harpyiai were depicted as winged women, sometimes with ugly faces or with the lower bodies of birds.
claims.statement_id: Para Harpyiai digambarkan sebagai wanita bersayap, kadang berwajah buruk atau bertubuh bawah burung.
claims.quote: The Harpyiai were depicted as winged women, sometimes with ugly faces, or with the lower bodies of birds.
